---
title: "Model and data files"
subtitle: "What an instance is, the 2-line and 3-line data files, and the 2016 swap"
---

## The model

A MultiZenoTravel instance ([§1.1 of the note](../proofs.qmd#node-s1-1)) has

- two hubs, the initial city $C_I$ and the goal city $C_G$, and $n$ central cities $1, \dots, n$;
- flights between a hub and a central city: $C_I$–$i$ lasts $d_i$, $i$–$C_G$ lasts $\bar d_i$,
  in both directions. There is no flight $C_I$–$C_G$. Central-to-central flights may exist;
- a landing cost $c_i$ in central city $i$ (landing in a hub is free);
- $p$ planes and $t \ge p$ passengers, all in $C_I$ at time 0. A plane carries at most one
  passenger, and boarding and debarking take no time.

A plan flies every passenger to $C_G$ and ends every plane in $C_G$. Its **cost** is the sum of its
landing costs and its **makespan** the time the last plane reaches $C_G$. The front is the set of
Pareto-optimal (cost, makespan) pairs over all plans, which may wait anywhere, hand passengers over
anywhere, and use central flights ([§1.2](../proofs.qmd#node-s1-2)). Every plan lands at least
$s = 2t - p$ times in central cities ([Lemma 3.2](../proofs.qmd#node-lemma-3-2)).

What `zeno` stores is `d`, `dbar`, `c`, `t` and `p`; durations, costs and times are non-negative
integers. The assumptions ([§1.4](../proofs.qmd#node-s1-4)) are

- **(S)**, symmetry: $d_i = \bar d_i$ for every city. Every instance the generator builds without
  `-E`/`-W` is symmetric;
- **(A1)**, under (S): central flights are no faster than through a hub, $d_{ij} \ge d_i + d_j$.
  Every PDDL problem `zeno` writes satisfies it (central flights last
  $\max(d_i, \bar d_i) + \max(d_j, \bar d_j) + 100$);
- **(A1-NS)**, the non-symmetric version: $d_{ij} \ge \min(d_i + d_j, \bar d_i + \bar d_j)$;
- **(AΔ)**, the triangle inequality on the flights that exist:
  $\mathrm{dur}(a, b) \le \mathrm{dur}(a, x) + \mathrm{dur}(x, b)$.

The front `zeno` prints is exact for symmetric instances under (A1), and by the note's
[Corollary 4.12](../proofs.qmd#node-corollary-4-12) under (AΔ) as well. For non-symmetric ones it
is exact wherever the certified bracket closes, under (A1-NS) when a bound needs it
([command line](../solver/cli.qmd#front)).

## Data files {#data-files}

`-d FILE` reads the durations and costs from a file instead of the generator. `-n` must still be
given and must match the file. Two layouts:

**2 lines, symmetric:** durations, then costs.

```text
6 10
40 20
```

This is `tests/golden/data/lpt-counterexample.dat`: $d = (6, 10)$, $c = (40, 20)$. With
`-n 2 -t 5 -p 2` it is the smallest instance on which the 2016 greedy misses a front point
([§5](../proofs.qmd#node-s5)).

**3 lines, possibly non-symmetric:** $C_I$-side durations $d$, $C_G$-side durations $\bar d$,
costs.

```text
3 19
3 11
5 1
```

This is the instance of [Proposition 6.5](../proofs.qmd#node-proposition-6-5)
(`zeno -n 2 -t 7 -p 4 -d prop65.dat`), on which waiting is harmful. A 3-line file with equal
first and second lines is symmetric.

Reading rules (`src/zeno/legacy_input.cpp`):

- tokens are separated by whitespace, and every non-blank line must have exactly $n$ of them;
  blank lines are skipped, so a trailing newline or blank line is harmless (the golden instance
  `trailing-newline` checks it);
- each token is read as an integer (`std::stoi`): `3.7` reads as 3, and a token that does not
  start with a number is an error;
- the file must have 2 or 3 non-blank lines;
- every value is then multiplied by `-r` (default 1) and truncated toward zero, as for generated
  instances, and negative values are rejected.

`zeno generate` writes the current instance in this format ([command line](../solver/cli.qmd#generate)).

## The 2016 swap {#swap}

::: {.callout-warning}
After reading or generating the vectors, if $n > 1$ and **the first duration exceeds the second**,
$d_1 > d_2$, `zeno` **exchanges the durations and the costs**, and reverses the $C_G$-side
durations. The 2016 code assumed increasing durations and did this, and `zeno` keeps it so that
both build the same instance from the same options.
:::

The rule, from `legacy::buildInstance`:

```cpp
if(n > 1 && d[0] > d[1])
{
    std::swap(d, c);           // durations <-> costs
    std::ranges::reverse(de);  // C_G-side durations reversed
}
if(symmetric)
    de = d;
```

Consequences:

- **2-line file.** A file `5 3` / `1 2` is solved as durations $(1, 2)$ and costs $(5, 3)$.
  `zeno front` prints a note on stderr when this happens to a data file:

  ```text
  zeno: note: the first duration exceeds the second, so the duration and cost lines of FILE were swapped, as the 2016 solvers did (order the cities to avoid it)
  ```

  `zeno pddl` and `zeno generate` apply the same swap without the note.
- **3-line file.** The swap is worse: $d$ and $c$ are exchanged and $\bar d$ is reversed, so
  each city gets another city's $C_G$-side duration. The file `5 3` / `7 8` / `1 2` becomes
  $d = (1, 2)$, $\bar d = (8, 7)$, $c = (5, 3)$.
- **The generator.** It computes durations on decreasing arguments, so for an increasing
  generating function the first duration is the largest and the swap fires. Then `-C` sets the
  *durations* and `-D` the *costs* ([generator](generator.qmd)). This is why the default instances
  have $d_i = i$ and $c_i = n + 1 - i$.
- **Ties.** After truncation the first two durations may be equal, and then nothing is swapped.
  `-n 10 -D 1` (log, `-r 1`) gives $d = (2, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0)$ and $c = (1, \dots, 10)$,
  whereas `-n 10 -D 1 -r 100` swaps and gives $d = (100, 200, \dots, 1000)$. The meaning of `-C`
  and `-D` thus depends on `-r`.
- **Round trips.** `zeno generate` writes the instance after the swap. If that instance still has
  $d_1 > d_2$, reading the file back swaps it again.

**To avoid the trap, order the cities by duration** so that $d_1 \le d_2$ (any order of the
others is fine), and check the instance with `zeno generate ... -d FILE` before solving it.
